entries.a710fff89822fed936900100cd13f519ee577a8d: <div sID="gen2530" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="20" osisID="Lev.20" sID="Lev.20"/> <div eID="gen2530" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2531" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen2532" type="x-p"/> The laws which before were made are in this chapter repeated and penalties annexed to them, that those who would not be deterred from sin by the fear of God might be deterred from it by the fear of punishment. If we will not avoid such and such practices because the law has made them sin (and it is most acceptable when we go on that principle of religion), surely we shall avoid them when the law has made them death, from a principle of self-preservation. In this chapter we have, I. Many particular crimes that are made capital. I. Giving their children to Moloch, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.1-Lev.20.5">ver. 1-5</reference>. 2. Consulting witches, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.6">ver. 6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.27">27</reference>. 3. Cursing parents, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.9">ver. 9</reference>. 4. Adultery, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.10">ver. 10</reference>. 5. Incest, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.11-Lev.20.12 Lev.20.14 Lev.20.17 Lev.20.19-Lev.20.21">ver. 11, 12, 14, 17, 19-21</reference>. 6. Unnatural lusts, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.13">ver. 13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.15">15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.16">16,</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.18">18</reference>. II. General commands given to be holy, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.7-Lev.20.8">ver. 7, 8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.22-Lev.20.26">22-26</reference>.
entries.be73544eeca3aa1036140e1e0bee308f49cc7c32: <div eID="gen2532" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen2531" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">Moral Laws. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 1490.)</title> <div sID="gen2533" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> And the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> spake unto Moses, saying, <hi type="super">2</hi> Again, thou shalt say to the children of Israel, Whosoever <hi type="italic">he be</hi> of the children of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn in Israel, that giveth <hi type="italic">any</hi> of his seed unto Molech; he shall surely be put to death: the people of the land shall stone him with stones. <hi type="super">3</hi> And I will set my face against that man, and will cut him off from among his people; because he hath given of his seed unto Molech, to defile my sanctuary, and to profane my holy name. <hi type="super">4</hi> And if the people of the land do any ways hide their eyes from the man, when he giveth of his seed unto Molech, and kill him not: <hi type="super">5</hi> Then I will set my face against that man, and against his family, and will cut him off, and all that go a whoring after him, to commit whoredom with Molech, from among their people. <hi type="super">6</hi> And the soul that turneth after such as have familiar spirits, and after wizards, to go a whoring after them, I will even set my face against that soul, and will cut him off from among his people. 7 Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy: for I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> your God. <hi type="super">8</hi> And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> which sanctify you. <hi type="super">9</hi> For every one that curseth his father or his mother shall be surely put to death: he hath cursed his father or his mother; his blood <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> upon him. <div eID="gen2533" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2534" type="x-p"/> Moses is here directed to say that again to the children of Israel which he had in effect said before, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.2">v. 2</reference>. We are sure it was no vain repetition, but very necessary, that they might <hi type="italic">give the more earnest heed to the things that were spoken,</hi> and might believe them to be of great consequence, being so often inculcated. <hi type="italic">God speaketh once, yea, twice,</hi> and what he orders to be said again we must be willing to hear again, because <hi type="italic">for us it is safe,</hi> <reference osisRef="Phil.3.1">Phil. iii. 1</reference>. <div eID="gen2534" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2535" type="x-p"/> I. Three sins are in these verses threatened with death:— <div eID="gen2535" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2536" type="x-p"/> 1. Parents abusing their children, by sacrificing them to Moloch, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.2-Lev.20.3">v. 2, 3</reference>. There is the grossest absurdity that can be in all the rites of idolatry, and they are all a great reproach to men's reason; but none trampled upon all the honours of human nature as this did, the burning of children in the fire to the honour of a dunghill-god. It was a plain evidence that their gods were devils, who desired and delighted in the misery and ruin of mankind, and that the worshippers were worse than the beasts that perish, perfectly stripped, not only of reason, but of natural affection. Abraham's offering Isaac could not give countenance, much less could it give rise to this barbarous practice, since, though that was commanded, it was immediately countermanded. Yet such was the power of the god of this world over the children of disobedience that this monstrous piece of inhumanity was generally practised; and even the Israelites were in danger of being drawn into it, which made it necessary that this severe law should be made against it. It was not enough to tell them they might spare their children (the fruit of their body should never be accepted for the sin of their soul), but they must be told, (1.) That the criminal himself should be put to death as a murderer: <hi type="italic">The people of the land shall stone him with stones</hi> (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.2">v. 2</reference>), which was looked upon as the worst of capital punishments among the Jews. If the children were sacrificed to the malice of the devil, the parents must be sacrificed to the justice of God. And, if either the fact could not be proved or the magistrates did not do their duty, God would take the work into his own hands: <hi type="italic">I will cut him off,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.3">v. 3</reference>. Note, Those that escape punishment from men, yet shall not escape the righteous judgments of God; so wretchedly do those deceive themselves that promise themselves impunity in sin. How can those escape against whom God sets his face, that is, whom he frowns upon, meets as an enemy, and fights against? The heinousness of the crime is here set forth to justify the doom: it <hi type="italic">defiles the sanctuary,</hi> and <hi type="italic">profanes the holy name</hi> of God, for the honour of both which he is jealous. Observe, The malignity of the sin is laid upon that in it which was peculiar to Israel. When the Gentiles sacrificed their children they were guilty of murder and idolatry; but, if the Israelites did it, they incurred the additional guilt of defiling the sanctuary (which they attended upon even when they lay under this guilt, as if there might be an agreement between the temple of God and idols), and of <hi type="italic">profaning the holy name of God,</hi> by which they were called, as if he allowed his worshippers to do such things, <reference osisRef="Rom.2.23">Rom. ii. 23, 24</reference>. (2.) That all his aiders and abetters should be cut off likewise by the righteous hand of God. If his neighbours concealed him, and would not come in as witnesses against him,—if the magistrates connived at him, and would not pass sentence upon him, rather pitying his folly than hating his impiety,—God himself would reckon with them, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.4-Lev.20.5">v. 4, 5</reference>. Misprision of idolatry is a crime cognizable in the court of heaven, and which shall not go unpunished: <hi type="italic">I will set my face against that man</hi> (that magistrate, <reference osisRef="Jer.5.1">Jer. v. 1</reference>) <hi type="italic">and against his family.</hi> Note, [1.] The wickedness of the master of a family often brings ruin upon a family; and he that should be the house-keeper proves the house-breaker. [2.] If magistrates will not do justice upon offenders, God will do justice upon them, because there is danger that many will <hi type="italic">go a whoring after those</hi> who do but countenance sin by winking at it. And, if the sins of leaders be leading sins, it is fit that their punishments should be exemplary punishments. <div eID="gen2536" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2537" type="x-p"/> 2. Children's abusing their parents, by cursing them, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.9">v. 9</reference>. If children should speak ill of their parents, or wish ill to them, or carry it scornfully or spitefully towards them, it was an iniquity to be punished by the judges, who were employed as conservators both of God's honour and of the public peace, which were both attacked by this unnatural insolence. See <reference osisRef="Prov.30.17">Prov. xxx. 17</reference>, <hi type="italic">The eye that mocks at his father the ravens of the valley shall pick out,</hi> which intimates that such wicked children were in a fair way to be not only hanged, but hanged in chains. This law of Moses Christ quotes and confirms (<reference osisRef="Matt.15.4">Matt. xv. 4</reference>), for it is as direct a breach of the fifth commandment as wilful murder is of the sixth. The same law which requires parents to be tender of their children requires children to be respectful to their parents. He that despitefully uses his parents, the instruments of his being, flies in the face of God himself, the author of his being, who will not see the paternal dignity and authority insulted and trampled upon. <div eID="gen2537" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2538" type="x-p"/> 3. Persons abusing themselves by consulting such as have <hi type="italic">familiar spirits,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.6">v. 6</reference>. By this, as much as any thing, a man diminishes, disparages, and deceives himself, and so abuses himself. What greater madness can there be than for a man to go to a liar for information, and to an enemy for advice? Those do so who turn after those that deal in the black art, and know the depths of Satan. This is spiritual adultery as much as idolatry is, giving that honour to the devil which is due to God only; and the jealous God will give a bill of divorce to those that thus <hi type="italic">go a whoring from him,</hi> and will <hi type="italic">cut them off,</hi> they having first cut themselves off from him. <div eID="gen2538" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2539" type="x-p"/> II. In the midst of these particular laws comes in that general charge, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.7-Lev.20.8">v. 7, 8</reference>, where we have, <div eID="gen2539" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2540" type="x-p"/> 1. The duties required; and they are two:— (1.) That in our principles, affections, and aims, we be holy: <hi type="italic">Sanctify yourselves and be you holy.</hi> We must cleanse ourselves from all the pollutions of sin, consecrate ourselves to the service and honour of God, and conform ourselves in every thing to his holy will and image: this is to <hi type="italic">sanctify ourselves.</hi> (2.) That in all our actions, and in the whole course of our conversation, we be obedient to the laws of God: <hi type="italic">You shall keep my statutes.</hi> By this only can we make it to appear that we have sanctified ourselves and are holy, even by our keeping God's commandments; <hi type="italic">the tree is known by its fruit.</hi> Nor can we <hi type="italic">keep God's statutes,</hi> as we ought, unless we first sanctify ourselves, and be holy. Make the tree good, and the fruit will be good. <div eID="gen2540" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2541" type="x-p"/> 2. The reasons to enforce these duties. (1.) "<hi type="italic">I am the Lord your God;</hi> therefore be holy, that you may resemble him whose people you are, and may be pleasing to him. Holiness becomes his house and household." (2.) <hi type="italic">I am the Lord who sanctifieth you.</hi> God sanctified them by peculiar privileges, laws, and favours, which distinguished them from all other nations, and dignified them as a people set apart for God. He gave them his word and ordinances to be means of their sanctification, and his good Spirit to instruct them; therefore they must be holy, else they received the grace of God herein in vain. Note, [1.] God's people are, and must be, persons of distinction. God has distinguished them by his holy covenant, and therefore they ought to distinguish themselves by their holy conversation. [2.] God's sanctifying us is a good reason why we should sanctify ourselves, that we may comply with the designs of his grace, and not walk contrary to them. If it be the Lord that sanctifies us, we may hope the work shall be done, though it be difficult: the manner of expression is like that, <reference osisRef="2Cor.5.5">2 Cor. v. 5</reference>, <hi type="italic">He that hath wrought us for the self-same thing is God.</hi> And his grace is so far from superseding our care and endeavour that it most strongly engages and encourages them. <hi type="italic">Work out your salvation, for it is God that worketh in you.</hi>
entries.0dc63da940f91771cf02598ef8671683d771365e: <div eID="gen2541" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2542" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">10</hi> And the man that committeth adultery with <hi type="italic">another</hi> man's wife, <hi type="italic">even he</hi> that committeth adultery with his neighbour's wife, the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death. <hi type="super">11</hi> And the man that lieth with his father's wife hath uncovered his father's nakedness: both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> upon them. <hi type="super">12</hi> And if a man lie with his daughter in law, both of them shall surely be put to death: they have wrought confusion; their blood <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> upon them. <hi type="super">13</hi> If a man also lie with mankind, as he lieth with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination: they shall surely be put to death; their blood <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> upon them. <hi type="super">14</hi> And if a man take a wife and her mother, it <hi type="italic">is</hi> wickedness: they shall be burnt with fire, both he and they; that there be no wickedness among you. <hi type="super">15</hi> And if a man lie with a beast, he shall surely be put to death: and ye shall slay the beast. <hi type="super">16</hi> And if a woman approach unto any beast, and lie down thereto, thou shalt kill the woman, and the beast: they shall surely be put to death; their blood <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> upon them. <hi type="super">17</hi> And if a man shall take his sister, his father's daughter, or his mother's daughter, and see her nakedness, and she see his nakedness; it <hi type="italic">is</hi> a wicked thing; and they shall be cut off in the sight of their people: he hath uncovered his sister's nakedness; he shall bear his iniquity. <hi type="super">18</hi> And if a man shall lie with a woman having her sickness, and shall uncover her nakedness; he hath discovered her fountain, and she hath uncovered the fountain of her blood: and both of them shall be cut off from among their people. <hi type="super">19</hi> And thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy mother's sister, nor of thy father's sister: for he uncovereth his near kin: they shall bear their iniquity. <hi type="super">20</hi> And if a man shall lie with his uncle's wife, he hath uncovered his uncle's nakedness: they shall bear their sin; they shall die childless. <hi type="super">21</hi> And if a man shall take his brother's wife, it <hi type="italic">is</hi> an unclean thing: he hath uncovered his brother's nakedness; they shall be childless. <div eID="gen2542" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2543" type="x-p"/> Sins against the seventh commandment are here ordered to be severely punished. These are sins which, of all others, fools are most apt to make a mock at; but God would teach those the heinousness of the guilt by the extremity of the punishment that would not otherwise be taught it. <div eID="gen2543" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2544" type="x-p"/> I. Lying with another man's wife was made a capital crime. The adulterer and the adulteress that had joined in the sin must fall alike under the sentence: they shall both be <hi type="italic">put to death,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.10">v. 10</reference>. Long before this, even in Job's time, this was reputed a <hi type="italic">heinous crime</hi> and an <hi type="italic">iniquity to be punished by the judges,</hi> <reference osisRef="Job.31.11">Job xxxi. 11</reference>. It is a presumptuous contempt of an ordinance of God, and a violation of his covenant, <reference osisRef="Prov.2.17">Prov. ii. 17</reference>. It is an irreparable wrong to the injured husband, and debauches the mind and conscience of both the offenders as much as any thing. It is a sin which headstrong and unbridled lusts hurry men violently to, and therefore it needs such a powerful restraint as this. It is a sin which defiles a land and brings down God's judgments upon it, which disquiets families, and tends to the ruin of all virtue and religion, and therefore is fit to be animadverted upon by the conservators of the public peace: but see <reference osisRef="John.8.3-John.8.11">John viii. 3-11</reference>. <div eID="gen2544" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2545" type="x-p"/> II. Incestuous connections, whether by marriage or not. 1. Some of them were to be punished with death, as a man's <hi type="italic">lying with his father's wife,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.11">v. 11</reference>. Reuben would have been put to death for his crime (<reference osisRef="Gen.35.22">Gen. xxxv. 22</reference>) if this law had been then made. It was the sin of the incestuous Corinthian, for which he was to be <hi type="italic">delivered unto Satan,</hi> <reference osisRef="1Cor.5.1">1 Cor. v. 1</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.5.5">5</reference>. A man's debauching his daughter-in-law, or his mother-in-law, or his sister, was likewise to be punished with death, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.12">v. 12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.14">14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.17">17</reference>. 2. Others of them God would punish with the curse of barrenness, as a man's defiling his aunt, or his brother's wife (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.19-Lev.20.21">v. 19-21</reference>): <hi type="italic">They shall die childless.</hi> Those that keep not within the divine rules of marriage forfeit the blessings of marriage: <hi type="italic">They shall commit whoredom, and shall not increase,</hi> <reference osisRef="Hos.4.10">Hos. iv. 10</reference>. Nay it is said, <hi type="italic">They shall bear their iniquity,</hi> that is, though they be not immediately cut off by the hand either of God or man for this sin, yet the guilt of it shall lie upon them, to be reckoned for another day, and not be purged with sacrifice or offering. <div eID="gen2545" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2546" type="x-p"/> III. The unnatural lusts of sodomy and bestiality (sins not to be mentioned without horror) were to be punished with death, as they are at this day by our law, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.13">v. 13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.15">15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.16">16</reference>. Even the beast that was thus abused was to be killed with the sinner, who was thereby openly put to the greater shame: and the villany was thus represented as in the highest degree execrable and abominable, all occasions of the remembrance or mention of it being to be taken away. Even the unseasonable use of the marriage, if presumptuous, and in contempt of the law, would expose the offenders to the just judgment of God: they <hi type="italic">shall be cut off,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.18">v. 18</reference>. For this is the will of God, that <hi type="italic">every man should possess his vessel</hi> (and the wife is called the weaker vessel) <hi type="italic">in sanctification and honour,</hi> as becomes saints.
entries.3393a76e853d20726979d0fa594452971d885d2f: <div eID="gen2546" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2547" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">22</hi> Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all my judgments, and do them: that the land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out. <hi type="super">23</hi> And ye shall not walk in the manners of the nation, which I cast out before you: for they committed all these things, and therefore I abhorred them. <hi type="super">24</hi> But I have said unto you, Ye shall inherit their land, and I will give it unto you to possess it, a land that floweth with milk and honey: I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> your God, which have separated you from <hi type="italic">other</hi> people. <hi type="super">25</hi> Ye shall therefore put difference between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean fowls and clean: and ye shall not make your souls abominable by beast, or by fowl, or by any manner of living thing that creepeth on the ground, which I have separated from you as unclean. <hi type="super">26</hi> And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> <hi type="italic">am</hi> holy, and have severed you from <hi type="italic">other</hi> people, that ye should be mine. <hi type="super">27</hi> A man also or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, shall surely be put to death: they shall stone them with stones: their blood <hi type="italic">shall be</hi> upon them. <div eID="gen2547" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2548" type="x-p"/> The last verse is a particular law, which comes in after the general conclusion, as if omitted in its proper place: it is for the putting of those to death that dealt with familiar spirits, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.27">v. 27</reference>. It would be an affront to God and to his lively oracles, a scandal to the country, and a temptation to ignorant bad people, to consult them, if such were known and suffered to live among them. Those that are in league with the devil have in effect made a covenant with death and an agreement with hell, and so shall their doom be. <div eID="gen2548" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2549" type="x-p"/> The rest of these verses repeat and inculcate what had been said before; for to that unthinking forgetful people it was requisite that there should be line upon line, and that general rules, with their reasons, should be frequently insisted on, for the enforcement of particular laws, and making them more effectual. Three things we are here reminded of:— <div eID="gen2549" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2550" type="x-p"/> I. Their dignity. 1. They had the <hi type="italic">Lord for their God,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.24">v. 24</reference>. They were his, his care, his choice, his treasure, his jewels, his kingdom of priests (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.26">v. 26</reference>): <hi type="italic">That you should be mine.</hi> Happy the people, and truly great, that are in such a case. 2. Their God was a holy God (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.26">v. 26</reference>), infinitely advanced above all others. His holiness is his glory, and it was their honour to be related to him, while their neighbours were the infamous worshippers of impure and filthy spirits. 3. The great God had separated them from other people (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.24">v. 24</reference>), and again, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.26">v. 26</reference>. Other nations were the common; they were the enclosure, beautified and enriched with peculiar privileges, and designed for peculiar honours; let them therefore value themselves accordingly, preserve their honour, and not lay it in the dust, by walking in the way of the heathen. <div eID="gen2550" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2551" type="x-p"/> II. Their duty; this is inferred from their dignity. God had done more for them than for others, and therefore expected more from them than from others. And what is it that the Lord their God requires, in consideration of the great things done and designed? 1. <hi type="italic">You shall keep all my statutes</hi> (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.22">v. 22</reference>); and there was all the reason in the world that they should, for the statutes were their honour, and obedience to them would be their lasting comfort. 2. <hi type="italic">You shall not walk in the manners of nations,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.23">v. 23</reference>. Being separated from them, they must not associate with them, nor learn their ways. The manners of the nations were bad enough in them, but would be much worse in God's people. 3. You shall <hi type="italic">put a difference between clean and unclean,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.25">v. 25</reference>. This is holiness, to discern between things that differ, not to live at large, as if we might say and do any thing, but to speak and act with caution. 4. <hi type="italic">You shall not make your souls abominable,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.25">v. 25</reference>. Our constant care must be to preserve the honour, by preserving the purity, of our own souls, and never to do any thing to make them abominable to God and to our own consciences. <div eID="gen2551" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen2552" type="x-p"/> III. Their danger. 1. They were going into an infected place (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.24">v. 24</reference>): <hi type="italic">You shall inherit their land,</hi> a land <hi type="italic">flowing with milk and honey,</hi> which they would have the comfort of if they kept their integrity; but, withal, it was a land full of idols, idolatries, and superstitious usages, which they would be apt to fall in love with, having brought from Egypt with them a strange disposition to take that infection. 2. If they took the infection, it would be of pernicious consequence to them. The Canaanites were to be expelled for these very sins: <hi type="italic">They committed all these things, therefore I abhorred them,</hi> <reference osisRef="Lev.20.23">v. 23</reference>. See what an evil thing sin is; it provokes God to abhor his own creatures, whereas otherwise he delights in the work of his hands. And, if the Israelites trod in the steps of their impiety, they must expect that the land would spue them out (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.22">v. 22</reference>), as he had told them before, <reference osisRef="Lev.18.28">ch. xviii. 28</reference>. If God spared not the natural branches, but broke them off, neither would he spare those who were grafted in, if they degenerated. Thus the rejection of the Jews stands for a warning to all Christian churches to take heed lest the kingdom of God be taken from them. Those that sin like others must expect to smart like them; and their profession of relation to God will be no security to them.  <chapter eID="Lev.20"/> <div eID="gen2552" type="x-p"/>

entries.74485db9d82a04a3db67f517926b21ec4484cd29: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1147"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 20</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Lev.20.1-Lev.20.27">Le 20:1-27</reference>. Giving One's Seed to Molech.</title> <div sID="gen1575" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1147"/><hi type="bold">2. Whosoever ... giveth any of his seed unto Molech--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Lev.18.21">Le 18:21</reference>).<div eID="gen1575" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1576" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the people of the land shall stone him with stones, &c.--</hi>Criminals who were condemned to be stoned were led, with their hands bound, without the gates to a small eminence, where was a large stone placed at the bottom. When they had approached within ten cubits of the spot, they were exhorted to confess, that, by faith and repentance, their souls might be saved. When led forward to within four cubits, they were stripped almost naked, and received some stupefying draught, during which the witnesses prepared, by laying aside their outer garments, to carry into execution the capital sentence which the law bound them to do. The criminal, being placed on the edge of the precipice, was then pushed backwards, so that he fell down the perpendicular height on the stone lying below: if not killed by the fall, the second witness dashed a large stone down upon his breast, and then the "people of the land," who were by-standers, rushed forward, and with stones completed the work of death (<reference osisRef="Matt.21.44">Mt 21:44</reference>; <reference osisRef="Acts.7.58">Ac 7:58</reference>). <div eID="gen1576" type="x-p"/>
entries.a48ab01c478a4df103f02187ec84fb1c0e811f7b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1148"/><div sID="gen1577" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1148"/><hi type="bold">4. If the people of the land do any ways hide their eyes from the man, &c.--</hi>that is, connive at their countrymen practising the horrid rites of Molech. Awful was it that any Hebrew parents could so violate their national covenant, and no wonder that God denounced the severest penalties against them and their families. <div eID="gen1577" type="x-p"/>
entries.0303a35d3978e63145b139d2ef87e4a31817875d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1149"/><div sID="gen1578" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1149"/><hi type="bold">7-19. Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy--</hi>The minute specification of the incestuous and unnatural crimes here enumerated shows their sad prevalence amongst the idolatrous nations around, and the extreme proneness of the Israelites to follow the customs of their neighbors. It is to be understood, that, whenever mention is made that the offender was "to be put to death" without describing the mode, stoning is meant. The only instance of another form of capital punishment occurs in <reference osisRef="Lev.20.14">Le 20:14</reference>, that of being burnt with fire; and yet it is probable that even here death was first inflicted by stoning, and the body of the criminal afterwards consumed by fire (<reference osisRef="Josh.7.15">Jos 7:15</reference>). <div eID="gen1578" type="x-p"/>
entries.da738ad5b1323782dcff3e60612783cca3c4a2d7: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1150"/><div sID="gen1579" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1150"/><hi type="bold">20. they shall die childless--</hi>Either by the judgment of God they shall have no children, or their spurious offspring shall be denied by human authority the ordinary privileges of children in Israel. <div eID="gen1579" type="x-p"/>
entries.0ce675a14f9dcb510ece007aae7cd7a330a4fc73: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv1151"/><div sID="gen1580" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv1151"/><hi type="bold">24. I ... have separated you from other people--</hi>Their selection from the rest of the nations was for the all-important end of preserving the knowledge and worship of the true God amid the universal apostasy; and as the distinction of meats was one great means of completing that separation, the law about making a difference between clean and unclean beasts is here repeated with emphatic solemnity. <chapter eID="Lev.20"/>

entries.07473aa6e0f05b1ad4326613a2bbc33aaa047367: <div eID="gen4906" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen4907" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen4908" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen4908" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen4907" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen4909" type="x-p"/> Of giving seed to Molech, and the punishment of this crime, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.1-Lev.20.5">Lev 20:1-5</reference>. Of consulting wizards, etc., <reference osisRef="Lev.20.6-Lev.20.8">Lev 20:6-8</reference>. Of disrespect to parents, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.9">Lev 20:9</reference>. Of adultery, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.10">Lev 20:10</reference>. Of incestuous mixtures, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.11">Lev 20:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.12">Lev 20:12</reference>. Bestiality, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.13-Lev.20.16">Lev 20:13-16</reference>. Different cases of incest and uncleanness, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.17-Lev.20.21">Lev 20:17-21</reference>. Exhortations and promises, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.22-Lev.20.24">Lev 20:22-24</reference>. The difference between clean and unclean animals to be carefully observed, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.25">Lev 20:25</reference>. The Israelites are separated from other nations, that they may be holy, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.26">Lev 20:26</reference>. A repetition of the law against wizards and them that have familiar spirits, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.27">Lev 20:27</reference>.
entries.c7d474258952d5011e090c72743760a7f120ddd4: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen4909" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4910" type="x-p"/> That giveth any of his seed unto Molech - To what has been said in the note on <reference osisRef="Lev.18.21">Lev 18:21</reference> (note), we may add, that the rabbins describe this idol, who was probably a representative or emblematical personification of the solar influence, as made of brass, in the form of a man, with the head of an ox; that a fire was kindled in the inside, and the child to be sacrificed to him was put in his arms, and roasted to death. Others say that the idol, which was hollow, was divided into seven compartments within; in one of which they put flour, in the second turtle-doves, in the third a ewe, in the fourth a ram, in the fifth a calf, in the sixth an ox, and in the seventh a child, which, by heating the statue on the outside, were all burnt alive together. I question the whole truth of these statements, whether from Jewish or Christian rabbins. There is no evidence of all this in the sacred writings. And there is but presumptive proof, and that not very strong, that human sacrifices were at all offered to Molech by the Jews. The passing through the fire, so frequently spoken of, might mean no more than a simple rite of consecration to the service of this idol. Probably a kind of ordeal was meant, the persons passing suddenly through the flame of a large fire, by which, though they might be burnt or scorched, yet they were neither killed nor consumed. Or they might have passed between two large fires, as a sort of purification. See the notes on <reference osisRef="Lev.20.14">Lev 20:14</reference>; See the notes on <reference osisRef="Lev.18.21">Lev 18:21</reference>. Caesar, in his history of the Gallic war, lib. vi., c. 16, mentions a custom of the Druids similar to this. They made an image of wickerwork, enclosed those in it whom they had adjudged to death, and, setting the whole on fire, all were consumed together.
entries.ee8a78ea565133cb9f63dfe9ad3bb2920b44e97b: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen4910" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4911" type="x-p"/> Familiar spirits - See the notes on <reference osisRef="Lev.19.31">Lev 19:31</reference>; and <reference osisRef="Exo.22.18">Exo 22:18</reference> (note).
entries.d74772d1b592061de840543df983745e034be582: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen4911" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4912" type="x-p"/> Curseth his father or his mother - See the notes on <reference osisRef="Gen.48.12">Gen 48:12</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Exo.20.12">Exo 20:12</reference> (note). He who conscientiously keeps the fifth commandment can be in no danger of this judgment. The term יקלל yekallel signifies, not only to curse, but to speak of a person contemptuously and disrespectfully, to make light of; so that all speeches which have a tendency to lessen our parents in the eyes of others, or to render their judgment, piety, etc., suspected and contemptible, may be here included; though the act of cursing, or of treating the parent with injurious and opprobrious language, is that which is particularly intended.
entries.3094e501ab44006a121e51ac276900328261e3af: <hi type="bold">Verse 10</hi> <div eID="gen4912" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4913" type="x-p"/> Committeth adultery - To what has been said in the note on See <reference osisRef="Exo.20.14">Exo 20:14</reference> (note), we may add, that the word adultery comes from the Latin adulterium, which is compounded of ad, to or with, and alter, another, or, according to Minshieu, of ad alterius forum, he that approaches to another man's bed.
entries.6c0b3851b7a7a9231ee59abf036e567b6523f540: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen4913" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4914" type="x-p"/> They have wrought confusion - See Leviticus 18, and especially the note on <reference osisRef="Lev.18.6">Lev 18:6</reference> (note).
entries.306d6cfafce344b334b3d7eb32840c6b83ee1e86: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen4914" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4915" type="x-p"/> They shall be burnt with fire - As there are worse crimes mentioned here, (see <reference osisRef="Lev.20.11">Lev 20:11</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.20.17">Lev 20:17</reference>), where the delinquent is ordered simply to be put to death, or to be cut off, it is very likely that the crime mentioned in this verse was not punished by burning alive, but by some kind of branding, by which they were ever after rendered infamous. I need not add that the original, באש ישרפו baesh yishrephu, may, without violence to its grammatical meaning, be understood as above, though in other places it is certainly used to signify a consuming by fire. But the case in question requires some explanation; it is this: a man marries a wife, and afterward takes his mother-in-law or wife's mother to wife also: now for this offense the text says all three shall be burnt with fire, and this is understood as signifying that they shall be burnt alive. Now the first wife, we may safely presume, was completely innocent, and was legally married: for a man may take to wife the daughter if single, or the mother if a widow, and in neither of these cases can any blame attach to the man or the party he marries; the crime therefore lies in taking both. Either, therefore, they were all branded as infamous persons, and this certainly was severe enough in the case of the first wife; or the man and the woman taken last were burnt: but the text says, both he and they; therefore, we should seek for another interpretation of they shall be burnt with fire, than that which is commonly given. Branding with a hot iron would certainly accomplish every desirable end both for punishment and prevention of the crime; and because the Mosaic laws are so generally distinguished by humanity, it seems to be necessary to limit the meaning of the words as above.
entries.286428a5f5b4f47bc4a01009cf03a5f144c2f11c: <hi type="bold">Verse 16</hi> <div eID="gen4915" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4916" type="x-p"/> If a woman approach unto any beast - We have the authority of one of the most eminent historians in the world, Herodotus, to say that this was a crime not unknown in Egypt; yea, that a case of this nature actually took place while he was there. Εγενετο δ' εν τῳ νο μῳ τουτῳ επ' εμευ τουτο το τερας, Γυναικι Τραγος εμισγετο αναφανδον. Τουτο ες επιδειξιν ανθρωπων απικετο. - Herod. in Euterp., p. 108. Edit. Gale, Lond. 1679. "In this district, within my own recollection, this portentous business took place: a goat coupled so publicly with a woman that every person knew it," etc. After this, need we wonder that God should have made laws of this nature, when it appears these abominations were not only practiced among the Egyptians, but were parts of a superstitious religious system? This one observation will account for many of those strange prohibitions which we find in the Mosaic law; others, the reasons of which are not so plain, we should see the propriety of equally, had we ampler historic records of the customs that existed in that country.
entries.6b83db2c46581ecbdb37d1a9a03b531903377a4c: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen4916" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4917" type="x-p"/> The land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out - See this energetic prosopopoeia explained in the note on <reference osisRef="Lev.18.25">Lev 18:25</reference> (note). From this we learn that the cup of the iniquities of the Canaanitish nations was full; and that, consistently with Divine justice, they could be no longer spared.
entries.d684779982a5e609dd8aff706935081d1e370c9a: <hi type="bold">Verse 24</hi> <div eID="gen4917" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4918" type="x-p"/> A land that floweth with milk and honey - See this explained <reference osisRef="Exo.3.8">Exo 3:8</reference> (note).
entries.af7b7f6b2380eba390059d708da0102e6943764b: <hi type="bold">Verse 25</hi> <div eID="gen4918" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4919" type="x-p"/> Between clean beasts and unclean - See the notes on Leviticus 11 (note).
entries.d62932c0b4ad26e382d888460be75820a86ea7cd: <hi type="bold">Verse 27</hi> <div eID="gen4919" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen4920" type="x-p"/> A familiar spirit - A spirit or demon, which, by magical rites, is supposed to be bound to appear at the call of his employer. See the notes on <reference osisRef="Gen.41.8">Gen 41:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exo.7.11">Exo 7:11</reference> (note), <reference osisRef="Exo.7.22">Exo 7:22</reference> (note), <reference osisRef="Exo.7.25">Exo 7:25</reference> (note); and <reference osisRef="Lev.19.31">Lev 19:31</reference> (note). From the accounts we have of the abominations both of Egypt and Canaan, we may blush for human nature; for wherever it is without cultivation, and without the revelation of God, it is every thing that is vile in principle and detestable in practice. Nor would any part of the habitable globe materially differ from Egypt and Canaan, had they not that rule of righteousness, the revealed Law of God, and had not life and immortality been brought to light by the Gospel among them. From these accounts, for which we could easily find parallels in ancient Greece and Italy, we may see the absolute need of a Divine revelation, without which man, even in his best estate, differs little from the brute.  <chapter eID="Lev.20"/> <div eID="gen4920" type="x-p"/>

entries.0f312e94b7cd32c514fcf968da4e9fceecba26fe: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.1">Lev 20:1</reference> <div eID="gen1426" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1427" type="x-p"/> Punishments for the Vices and crimes Prohibited in Ch. 18 and 19. - The list commences with idolatry and soothsaying, which were to be followed by extermination, as a practical apostasy from Jehovah, and a manifest breach of the covenant.
entries.192a29893792bb60a622c0366d31f51eda3803f0: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.2">Lev 20:2</reference> <div eID="gen1427" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1428" type="x-p"/> Whoever, whether an Israelite or a foreigner in Israel, dedicated of his seed (children) to Moloch (see <reference osisRef="Lev.18.21">Lev 18:21</reference>), was to be put to death. The people of the land were to stone him. בּאבן רגם, <hi type="italic">lapide obruere</hi>, is synonymous with סקל, lit., <hi type="italic">lapidem jacere:</hi> this was the usual punishment appointed in the law for cases in which death was inflicted, either as the result of a judicial sentence, or by the national community.
entries.55a3d07ccc0c9884b15820ea52fe92ce197e26b7: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.3">Lev 20:3</reference> <div eID="gen1428" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1429" type="x-p"/> By this punishment the nation only carried out the will of Jehovah; for He would cut off such a man (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.17.10">Lev 17:10</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.18.21">Lev 18:21</reference>) for having defiled the sanctuary of Jehovah and desecrated the name of Jehovah, not because he had brought the sacrifice to Moloch into the sanctuary of Jehovah, as <hi type="italic">Movers</hi> supposes, but in the same sense in which all the sins of Israel defiled the sanctuary in their midst (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.31">Lev 15:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.16.16">Lev 16:16</reference>).
entries.1ca96e55fa8f7164326b77118adc4baf7da49fad: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.4-Lev.20.5">Lev 20:4-5</reference> <div eID="gen1429" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1430" type="x-p"/> If the people, however (the people of the land), should hide their eyes from him (on the <hi type="italic">dagesh</hi> in חעלּם and יעלּימוּ see the note on <reference osisRef="Lev.4.13-Lev.4.21">Lev 4:13-21</reference>), from an unscrupulous indifference or a secret approval of his sin, the Lord would direct His face against him and his family, and cut him off with all that went a whoring after him.
entries.773112c1c9b02c423bc2cc3519dcd2d400b9d0d8: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.6">Lev 20:6</reference> <div eID="gen1430" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1431" type="x-p"/> He would also do the same to every soul that turned to familiar spirits and necromantists (<reference osisRef="Lev.19.31">Lev 19:31</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Exod.22.17">Exo 22:17</reference>), “to go a whoring after them,” i.e., to make himself guilty of idolatry by so doing, such practices being always closely connected with idolatry.
entries.cb270f6dfabd501423978c6cb2906c6245471b9f: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.7-Lev.20.8">Lev 20:7-8</reference> <div eID="gen1431" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1432" type="x-p"/> For the Israelites were to sanctify themselves, i.e., to keep themselves pure from all idolatrous abominations, to be holy because Jehovah was holy (<reference osisRef="Lev.11.44">Lev 11:44</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.19.2">Lev 19:2</reference>), and to keep the statutes of their God who sanctified them (<reference osisRef="Exod.31.13">Exo 31:13</reference>).
entries.ef654de80c6b6eadb9c7861b7d2e278b8b861890: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.9-Lev.20.18">Lev 20:9-18</reference> <div eID="gen1432" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1433" type="x-p"/> Whoever cursed father or mother was to be punished with death (<reference osisRef="Lev.19.3">Lev 19:3</reference>); “<hi type="italic">His blood would be upon him</hi>.” The cursing of parents was a capital crime (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.17.4">Lev 17:4</reference>, and for the plural דּמיו <reference osisRef="Exod.22.1">Exo 22:1</reference> and <reference osisRef="Gen.4.10">Gen 4:10</reference>), which was to return upon the doer of it, according to Gen 9:6. The same punishment was to be inflicted upon adultery (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.10">Lev 20:10</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.20">Lev 18:20</reference>), carnal intercourse with a father’s wife (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.11">Lev 20:11</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.7-Lev.18.8">Lev 18:7-8</reference>) or with a daughter-in-law (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.12">Lev 20:12</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.17">Lev 18:17</reference>), sodomy (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.13">Lev 20:13</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.22">Lev 18:22</reference>), sexual intercourse with a mother and her daughter, in which case the punishment was to be heightened by the burning of the criminals when put to death (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.14">Lev 20:14</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.17">Lev 18:17</reference>), lying with a beast (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.15">Lev 20:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.16">Lev 20:16</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.23">Lev 18:23</reference>), sexual intercourse with a half-sister (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.17">Lev 20:17</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.9">Lev 18:9</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.18.11">Lev 18:11</reference>), and lying with a menstruous woman (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.18">Lev 20:18</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.19">Lev 18:19</reference>). The punishment of death, which was to be inflicted in all these cases upon both the criminals, and also upon the beast that had been abused (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.15">Lev 20:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.16">Lev 20:16</reference>), was to be by stoning, according to <reference osisRef="Lev.20.2">Lev 20:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.27">Lev 20:27</reference>, and Deu 22:21.; and by the burning (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.14">Lev 20:14</reference>) we are not to understand death by fire, or burning alive, but, as we may clearly see from <reference osisRef="Josh.7.15">Jos 7:15</reference> and <reference osisRef="Josh.7.25">Jos 7:25</reference>, burning the corpse after death. This was also the case in <reference osisRef="Lev.21.9">Lev 21:9</reference> and Gen 38:24.
entries.ae5d2498e5493b9feea6fcd180bdfb5a4ebae0b5: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.19-Lev.20.21">Lev 20:19-21</reference> <div eID="gen1433" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1434" type="x-p"/> No civil punishment, on the other hand, to be inflicted by the magistrate or by the community generally, was ordered to follow marriage with an aunt, the sister of father or mother (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.19">Lev 20:19</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.12-Lev.18.13">Lev 18:12-13</reference>), with an uncle’s wife (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.20">Lev 20:20</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.4">Lev 18:4</reference>), or with a sister-in-law, a brother’s wife (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.21">Lev 20:21</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.16">Lev 18:16</reference>). In all these cases the threat is simply held out, “they shall bear their iniquity,” and (according to <reference osisRef="Lev.20.20">Lev 20:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.21">Lev 20:21</reference>) “die childless;” that is to say, God would reserve the punishment to Himself (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.18.14">Lev 18:14</reference>). In the list of punishments no reference is made to intercourse with a mother (<reference osisRef="Lev.18.7">Lev 18:7</reference>) or a granddaughter (<reference osisRef="Lev.18.10">Lev 18:10</reference>), as it was taken for granted that the punishment of death would be inflicted in such cases as these; just as marriage with a daughter or a full sister is passed over in the prohibitions in ch. 18.
entries.68907d28aff3d647dc49204313d29d451a551db4: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.22-Lev.20.26">Lev 20:22-26</reference> <div eID="gen1434" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1435" type="x-p"/> The list of punishments concludes, like the prohibitions in Lev 18:24., with exhortations to observe the commandments and judgments of the Lord, and to avoid such abominations (on <reference osisRef="Lev.18.22">Lev 18:22</reference> cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.3-Lev.18.5">Lev 18:3-5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.18.26">Lev 18:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.18.28">Lev 18:28</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.18.30">Lev 18:30</reference>; and on <reference osisRef="Lev.18.23">Lev 18:23</reference> cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.3">Lev 18:3</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.18.24">Lev 18:24</reference>). The reason assigned for the exhortations is, that Jehovah was about to give them for a possession the fruitful land, whose inhabitants He had driven out because of their abominations, and that Jehovah was their God, who had separated Israel from the nations. For this reason (<reference osisRef="Lev.18.25">Lev 18:25</reference>) they were also to sever (make distinctions) between clean and unclean cattle and birds, and not make their souls (i.e., their persons) abominable through unclean animals, with which the earth swarmed, and which God had “<hi type="italic">separated to make unclean,</hi>” i.e., had prohibited them from eating or touching when dead, because they defiled (see ch. 11). For (<reference osisRef="Lev.18.26">Lev 18:26</reference>) they were to be holy, because Jehovah their God was holy, who had severed them from the nations, to belong to Him, i.e., to be the nation of His possession (see <reference osisRef="Exod.19.4-Exod.19.6">Exo 19:4-6</reference>).
entries.be429d95fda6cc2eb30fe70d4644d673804a7ee1: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.27">Lev 20:27</reference> <div eID="gen1435" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1436" type="x-p"/> But because Israel was called to be the holy nation of Jehovah, every one, ether man or woman, in whom there was a heathenish spirit of soothsaying, was to be put to death, viz., stoned (cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.19.31">Lev 19:31</reference>), to prevent defilement by idolatrous abominations. Holiness of the Priests, of the Holy Gifts, and of Sacrifices - Leviticus 21-22 <div eID="gen1436" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1437" type="x-p"/> The Sanctification of the Priests. - As the whole nation was to strive after sanctification in all the duties of life, on account of its calling as a nation of God, the priests, whom Jehovah had chosen out of the whole nation to be the custodians of His sanctuary, and had sanctified to that end, were above all to prove themselves the sanctified servants of the Lord in their domestic life and the duties of their calling. (1) They were not to defile themselves by touching the dead or by signs of mourning (<reference osisRef="Lev.21.1-Lev.21.6">Lev 21:1-6</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.21.10-Lev.12.2">Lev 21:10-12); (2</reference>) they were to contract and maintain a spotless marriage (<reference osisRef="Lev.21.7-Lev.21.9">Lev 21:7-9</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.21.13-Lev.21.15">Lev 21:13-15</reference>); and (3) those members of the priesthood who had any bodily failings were to keep away from the duties of the priests’ office (<reference osisRef="Lev.21.16-Lev.21.24">Lev 21:16-24</reference>).  <chapter eID="Lev.20"/> <div eID="gen1437" type="x-p"/>

entries.b19c2eae4a5ebe820f117bc6707600cefd954f4c:
1. And the Lord spake. The prohibition of this superstition was previously expounded in its proper place. God here commands the punishment to be inflicted, if any one should have polluted himself with it. And surely it was a detestable sacrilege to enslave to idols that offspring, which was begotten to God, and which He had adopted in the loins of Abraham, since in this way they not only despoiled God of His right, but, so far as they could, blotted out the grace of adoption. What He had then generally pronounced, He now specially applies, viz., that they should be stoned who offered their seed to Molech; for otherwise they would have tried to escape on the pretense that they had no intention of revolting to other gods. Just as now-a-days, under the Papacy, whatever is alleged from Scripture against their impious and corrupt worship, is coldly and contemptuously received; because they varnish over their idolatries, and so indulge themselves in them in security. But after God has commanded His judges to punish this crime severely, He at the same time declares that, if perchance they should connive at it, and encourage it by their lenity, He Himself will avenge it, so as to punish much more heavily those who may have escaped from the hands of men; and not only so, but that He would implicate all those who might have been aware of it in the same con-detonation.

entries.b035b86da327b3eb5aa00b12d56bc25e5499e20b: <div annotateRef="Bible:Lev.20.11" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Lev.20.11" sID="gen15370" type="section"/><p/> <div sID="gen15371" type="x-p"/>Nothing new occurs here, for the object of Moses was, by the enactment of penalties, to sanction the instruction lately given. By previously condemning incestuous marriages, he would cite the Israelites before God, in order that their consciences might abhor the crime, although he gave them nothing to fear from earthly judges; whereas now he alarms them by the dread of punishment, in case any should indulge themselves with too great security. He does not chastise the incestuous with rods, as if they were only guilty of a light offense; but he pronounces it to be a capital crime, if any had sinned against the law of nature; and first he condemns the step-mother and step-son to death, if they should have had connection with each other; he then makes the same decree with reference to the father-in-law and daughter-in-law; and, thirdly, the step-father and step-daughter. But when, if a man cohabits at the same time with a mother and her daughter, he extends the punishment to the mother also, it must be understood, provided she also consents to the abominable medley; for, if a man, against the mother’s will, seduces her daughter, and the mother is unable to resist it if she would, she is free from guilt. The same punishment is awarded to brother and sister, and nephew and aunt, and it is extended also to affinity; if any should cohabit with the wife of his uncle or his brother. We have elsewhere explained the meaning of the expression, “their blood shall be upon them;” <hi type="italic">i</hi>.<hi type="italic">e</hi>., that the cause of their death is to be imputed to none but the gross criminals themselves, lest their judges, under the cloak of humanity, should shrink from being severe, since it often happens that those who do not sufficiently weigh the atrocity of the evil, are led away by an empty show of clemency. <note n="95"> <div sID="gen15372" type="x-p"/> “Sont ployables, et faciles a pardoner;” are pliable and easily disposed to pardon. — <hi type="italic">Fr</hi>.<div eID="gen15372" type="x-p"/> </note> Moreover, Moses indirectly hints that if the guilty be pardoned, vengeance will be thus provoked against the whole people, since iniquity is fostered by impunity, until it bursts out like a deluge. The penalty of childlessness corresponds with the crime, for it is just that those should be exterminated in barrenness from the world, who have endeavored to corrupt the holy race of Abraham with their adulterous seed.<div eID="gen15371" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Lev.20.11" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen15370" osisID="Lev.20.11" type="section"/>

God had hitherto taught what was right, in order to restrain the people from sin, not only from fear of punishment, but for conscience’ sake. But whereas all do not voluntarily dispose themselves to obedience, the awards severe punishments to those wicked despisers in whom there is no effort to be religious. And it is astonishing that almost all the Gentiles have so sunk into stupid and brutal folly, that they have tolerated with little less than impunity unnatural crimes, detestable in their very name.
I admit that even the wickedest of them were ashamed to justify so gross a crime; but although it was practiced with impunity, it was a common reproach to make even against the very public tribunals, that it ought to be more severely punished than other crimes, which they did not spare.
Both of the offending parties were subjected to the same punishment, because it is a pollution which ought by no means to be borne. Nay, if a man or woman offend with a beast, in order that, all may the more abhor and beware of the unnatural crime, the penalty is extended even to the harmless animal; as we have before seen that a goring ox is condemned to death if it had killed a man. Hence we infer how greatly displeasing to God is this kind of crime, since its iniquity is confirmed by the death of guiltless animals.

The enormity of the crime is seen by the severity of the punishment; and surely, when a man and woman abandon themselves to so disgraceful an act, it is plain that there are no remains of modesty in them. God, therefore, does not only regard the offense itself, but the brutal impulse of lust, whereby men are so carried away as to degenerate from the very feelings of nature. For what wickedness would he abstain from who yields to such impurity, that he breaks through an obstacle in his fury which restrains the brutes themselves? Let us not wonder, then, that God is a severe avenger of such obscenity.

entries.4b299e2ea4b72fc7e27e9e7e9dc87c55a3c73610: <div annotateRef="Bible:Lev.20.25" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Lev.20.25" sID="gen10364" type="section"/> <div sID="gen10365" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold"><reference osisRef="Bible:Lev.20.25">Leviticus 20:25</reference>. </hi><hi type="italic">Ye shall therefore put difference. </hi>I have no doubt but that this sentence depends on the end of the foregoing verse; for although that verse contains a reason to deter them from incest, of which he had been speaking, still it refers also to the doctrine before us, and stands in the shape of preface to it. In a word, it connects two things, for God here briefly declares His will, not only with respect to unlawful and improper intercourse, but also why He forbids His people to eat of unclean animals. Therefore He says, “I am the Lord your God, which have separated you from <hi type="italic">other </hi>people.” Whence it follows, that for no other reason were they prohibited from eating those animals, except that they thence may learn to take more diligent heed, and to withdraw themselves far from all the pollutions of the Gentiles. He had before recommended purity by various symbols, and now extends it even to the very animals. And this reason must be carefully marked, that the distinction between meats is propounded to them in order that they may study purity. For there would be something unmeaning in what is here said, if we did not know that this interdiction was imposed with this object, that they should not mix themselves promiscuously with the Gentiles. Therefore it is again repeated, that they were severed, that they might be God’s inheritance; and hence it is inferred, that holiness was to be cultivated by them, that they might conform themselves to the example of their God. Now it cannot be questioned, that the distinction of meats which is prescribed, is a supplement to the First Commandment, wherein the rule for worshipping God duly and purely is laid down; and thus                   <ns0:head>CHAP. XX.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 AND the LORD spake unto Moses, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 18. 21.</ns0:note> Again, thou shalt say to the children of Israel <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Here follow the punishments of the crimes forbidden in the former chapters.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 18. 10. 2 Kin. 17. 17. and 23. 10. Jer. 32. 35.</ns0:note>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Whosoever <ns0:hi>he be</ns0:hi> of the children of Israel, or of the strangers <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Not onely such as were Proselytes, but all others, these being gross immoralities<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and such as the precepts of <ns0:hi>Noah</ns0:hi> reached to, and such as the laws of nature and nations obliged them to. And therefore the toleration of such actions was not onely against reason of state and the interest of the com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monwealth of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> and dangerous to the infection and destru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ction of the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> by the imitation of such examples, but also against the light of nature and laws of humanity.</ns0:note> that sojourn in Israel, that giveth <ns0:hi>any</ns0:hi> of his seed unto Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lech <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Or to any other Idol, for the reason of the law equally concerns all. See <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 18. 21.</ns0:note>, he shall surely be put to death: the peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple of the land shall stone him with stones.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And I will set my face against that man <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Deal with him as an enemy, and make him a mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nument of my justice<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> either by punishing him immediately and eminently, when the Magistrate cannot or will not do it, or by adding to his corporal punishments my curse upon his soul and name. See <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 17. 10.</ns0:note>, and will cut him off from among his people <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">From the number of his people, of what nation or kindred soever he was, or, from the land of the living.</ns0:note>: because he hath given of his seed unto Molech, to defile my sanctuary <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Which was done by this wickedness, either be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause such persons did, for the cover of their Idolatry, come into Gods Sanctuary, as the rest did: See <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 15. 31. or be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause the Sanctuary was and was said to be defiled by gross abominations committed in that city or land where Gods Sanctuary was: or because by these actions they did pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nounce and declare to all men that they esteemed the san<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctuary and service of God abominable and vile, by preferring such odious and pernicious Idolatry before it.</ns0:note>, and to prophane my ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Name <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Partly by de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spising it themselves, and partly by disgracing it to others and giving them occasion to blaspheme it, and to abhor the true religion, because they saw it deserted and condemned by those that best knew it and once embraced it.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 And if the people of the land do any wayes hide their eyes from the man <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Wink at his fault, and forbear to accuse and punish him. Compare <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 17. 30.</ns0:note>, when he giveth of his seed unto Molech, and kill him not <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">

                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 Then I will set my face against that man, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 20. 5.</ns0:note> against his family <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Either 1. his posterity, whom God threatned to punish for their fathers Idolatry, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 20. Or 2. his people, as that word is used, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 8. 3. <ns0:hi>Mic.</ns0:hi> 2. 3. to wit, the people of that land, who by their connivance make themselves guilty of his sin, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 4. Or 3. his disciples and followers, who are oft called the sons or children of their masters. And so it may be seem to be explained in the following words, <ns0:hi>all that go a whoring after him,</ns0:hi> as the first clause which concerns the head or chief person himself, <ns0:hi>I will set my face against that man,</ns0:hi> is ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plained by these words, <ns0:hi>I will cut him off.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, and will cut him off, and all that go a whoring after him, to commit whoredom with Molech, from among their people.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 19. 31.</ns0:note>. the soul that turneth after such as have familiar spirits and after wizards, to go a whoring after them <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">To seek knowledge or counsel or help from them.</ns0:note>, I will even set my face a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst that soul, and will cut him off from among his people.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 11. 44. & 19. 2. 1 Pet, 1. 16.</ns0:note> Sanctifie your selves therefore, and be ye holy: for I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> LORD your God.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> the LORD which sanctifie you <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Who separated you from all nations and from their impurities and Idolatries to be a peculiar people to my self, and therefore I will not suffer you to follow their examples. Or, who really sanctify you, and give you my grace to do what I require, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> to keep my statutes. Or the argument is this, Those idols and Idolatries will defile you and make you worse, but I onely and my service will sanctify you and make you better.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 22. 22.                   <ns0:p n="11">11 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 18. 8.</ns0:note> And the man that lieth with his fathers wife, hath uncovered his fathers nakedness: both of them shall surely be put to death, their blood <ns0:hi>shall be</ns0:hi> upon them.</ns0:p>
